versions.title: Every kind of app, with the safety to match

items.text: News in the sidebar: what's new in each version, reports and articles, with a dot when something is new.
Design systems: pick one of six starters or measure one from a site or screenshot, and every chat in the project builds to it.
Comment on part of a page in the Browser tab: point at an element, say what should change, and the agent changes only that.
Export a page as a PDF or a full-length PNG, or the project's files as a ZIP.
Any MCP client can hand work to QuorX: list projects, start a reply, follow it and stop it, while approvals stay yours.
Replay a finished reply step by step with its real timing, a scrubber and speeds up to 16×.
Home's start box picks a project, a recent folder or a template before you type.
Projects show their GitHub repo, can be pinned or archived, and the chat header shows what the project has spent.
Costs update live while a reply runs, and a reply that ended early still counts what its calls spent.
The side panel can be hidden for a chat-only view, text size and page zoom are set separately, and notifications carry QuorX's name.
The agent works through a real shell, so it can build command-line programs and desktop apps, not only web pages.
Rules read every command before it runs; deleting your profile, a drive or a system folder is blocked however it is written.
Stop ends everything a command started and confirms nothing is left, and Undo now covers what commands change.
A tripwire stops a command part-way when many files outside the project disappear.
In YOLO the deciders vote on risky commands; they see only the facts, need a quorum, and never include the chat's own model.
Spending caps per reply and per day, and installs for the whole computer always ask you first.
QuorX checks that a toolchain can really build here before the agent starts, and says what is missing.
The agent can answer prompts in terminal programs, click through Windows desktop apps and Android emulators, and use a debugger.
A Running tab shows everything running in a project and who started it, with Stop on each and Stop all.
Long builds and installs move to the background instead of being cut off at a time limit.
Platform packs: one file per kind of app tells QuorX how to detect, check, run, debug and explain it.
Anyone can test the packs their computer supports with npm run test:packs, without an OpenRouter key.
.NET: WinForms and WPF apps are built and driven, dotnet test failures are summed up, and netcoredbg debugs them.
Scripts that run other programs are read first and always ask, so a wrapper script can't hide what really runs.
Tauri apps are built, and their window is read and clicked through WebView2.
Go, C, C++ and Rust programs can be debugged with breakpoints, and C and C++ projects get a build check before the reply.
Electron apps are driven through their DevTools port, and the debugger attaches to the main process.
Godot and Unity projects are checked and their tests summed up; MSIX and WiX installers are built with test certificates only.
Android emulators are started and driven, crashes point to your code's first line, and Flutter apps are checked and debugged.
Java and Kotlin: Gradle and Maven compile checks, JUnit summaries, and a debugger built on the JDK's own.
QuorX runs safely on macOS and Linux: Stop ends whole process groups, rules read bash and zsh, and key folders are off limits.
On a Mac, iPhone and Mac apps are built with Xcode, driven in the Simulator and debugged; crash reports are summed up.
Python desktop apps use the project's own virtual environment, and tkinter and PyQt windows are driven and debugged.
The update button in the sidebar is short and fills up like a progress bar while the update downloads.
With the sidebar folded, a waiting update shows as an icon above restart, theme and settings.
A reply no longer fails its final check when the hidden browser won't start; it uses the agent's own tab or checks the files.
QuorX finds Chrome installed for one user, 32-bit Chrome, Brave and Chromium, and says why a browser didn't start.
Pages the agent makes load from their own local address, so storage works in artifacts and project pages.
The side pane's tabs show only icons when the pane is narrow, and the servers button stays in view.
When the same problem comes back, a second model with a clean context finds the likely cause before the next try.
QuorX runs any model through OpenRouter, with a quorum of decider models behind its choices.
The agent builds web apps, sites and games, and opens each one in a browser to check it before it replies.
